Manchester United were thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as head coach after Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card; Red Devils have conceded 34 goals in all competitions this season - the most by any side in Europe's major leagues
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Gary Neville accused Manchester United's hierarchy of negligence for failing to strengthen their defence as their 4-0 loss to Liverpool left them with the worst defensive record in Europe.
Liverpool ran riot after Leny Yoro's eighth-minute red card at Anfield as goals from Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz ensured Mauricio Pochettino suffered a horror start to his Manchester United tenure.
United have now conceded 34 goals in all competitions this term. It is the highest total of any side across Europe's top-five leagues. The result keeps them second from bottom in the Premier League.
"The negligence is not bringing in defenders in the transfer window, because we've seen this for two or three years."
Pochettino made the decision to hand Matthijs de Ligt his first Premier League start in 357 days at Anfield but the Netherlands international was partly at fault for the opening goal and endured a torrid evening along with the rest of United's defenders.
Watching back the opener, when De Ligt misjudged a high ball, Neville said: "The minute that De Ligt makes that run in that channel, Yoro has to come across within 10 metres of him, and [Diogo] Dalot has to come across. This is so bad from Yoro and Dalot.
"De Lift makes a right mess of it. He can't believe it though, De Ligt. He's played centre-half before. He can't believe Yoro's not there. Then Yoro makes contact and it's clumsy.
"You've got a back four who are looking after their own jobs, they're in fear.
"De Ligt and Martinez have dropped off, Dalot's not coming quickly enough.
"It's a mess because of the fact they've got no confidence and haven't got the ability to play out there at Anfield in a game against Liverpool."
Neville was baffled by Pochettino's decision to start De Ligt, who was similarly poor when returning from injury in last month's 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League.
"We were in the trucks over in the compound and when the team came through straight away we were very surprised," added Neville.
"I just didn't think Manchester United would win, and I thought they would concede lots of goals and make mistakes.
"Maybe the options on the bench aren't brilliant either, but it's really desperate and it's tiring watching them.
"Mauricio Pochettino's options are not great, but I didn't get De Ligt.
"Having been out for a year myself, it's really difficult to come back into a game like that.
"I'm not saying that you can't, but as a centre-back getting your bearings… You saw him in Como, he was all over the place in Como.
"It's almost like you don't know what's happening. I found that coming back into it when I was 32, he's obviously more experienced as well.
"I was very surprised he played but then the others haven't been doing great either."
United's total of eight points after 11 games is their lowest at this stage of a season since the 1972/73 campaign.
"You wonder how low it can get, but this is as low as it's been in 54 years," added Neville.
"A few weeks ago against Fulham, I said it's the worst 40 minutes or 30 minutes I've seen in my lifetime.
"At the time people said that was maybe a bit too much, but this is actually the worst Manchester United have ever been in 54 years. It's a fact.
"The worst defensive team in Europe, second bottom in the league, they've never started this badly."
He added: "I would have started with Harry Maguire today. Manchester United's best back four - and I think we're informed enough to know, we've watched these lads for two or three years - is [Luke] Shaw, Dalot, Maguire and [Lisandro] Martinez.
"Now, it's a poor back four, let me be really clear. But it is Manchester United's best back four.
"Now, if you can get that back four out on the pitch, it does win games, against Liverpool last year, it does win games against City and Arsenal, it can compete slightly.
"But that back four that started today, and the one that finished against Villa a few weeks ago of [Noussair] Mazraoui, [Patrick] Dorgu, Yoro, and [Ayden] Heaven - that will get you relegated, that's a fact."

Arsenal were booed by their fans after they held to a sixth successive draw at home, drawing 0-0 with West Ham in the Women's Super League.
The Hammers avoided defeat to the Gunners for the first time to pile the pressure on Renee Slegers and her side, who now have just 15 points after 11 games and sit in sixth.
Arsenal had 22 shots in total, with 67 per cent possession, but did not create one big chance throughout.
The best chance of the game came through substitute Kyra Cooney-Cross when her shot struck the post following a big deflection.
But, overall, it was another tepid display in front of the home crowd, and those in red did not do enough to finally emerge with three points.
The well-deserved point for West Ham takes them above Liverpool into 12th.
Manchester United left it very late to claim a 2-1 victory over Birmingham.
Geum-Min Lee put struggling Birmingham in front in only the fourth minute and United struggled to create clear-cut chances, while Phallon Tullis-Joyce made a couple of crucial saves.
The visitors finally found the breakthrough 10 minutes from time through Elisabeth Terland, and Simi Awujo broke Birmingham hearts with a header four minutes into added time.
Bottom-side Charlton claimed their first point of the season at the 11th time of asking with a 1-1 draw against Aston Villa.
Keira Flannery put Charlton ahead with a first-half penalty but Lucy Parker pulled Villa level 19 minutes from time.
An early own goal scored by Maz Pacheco saw struggling Everton fall to a 1-0 defeat at home to Brighton.
Earlier on Sunday, Manchester City saw their 17-game winning league run at the Joie Stadium come to an end with a 3-1 defeat to Tottenham.
Renee Slegers speaking after Arsenal's 0-0 draw with West Ham on whether she is considering her future:
"I love the club. I'm very passionate about this group of players, we're going through a very difficult time, and I take my responsibilities because the results haven't been good enough.
"In the second half we are chasing again but we're not creating good enough chances to the final third, from all phases, and the way we get there, it's not the Arsenal standard and we need to do that better. But I take my responsibilities in my role.
"That [fans booing] is on us and that's our responsibility. That it's so quiet in the stadium because we don't inspire enough. We don't bring enough energy.
"I think, about the fans, because it's cold and they want to see good football and get inspired today and that's not what we did. And at the end of the day, that's my responsibility.
"That doesn't feel good. The fans booing at the end, they care and they want more from this team, which the group is determined to turn things around.
"It's very tough for the players and the players that have been at Arsenal for longer, or even the players that came last year. No one has gone through this ever with Arsenal.
"The group has been great. They've been very good in the situation but, of course, it's the last one of the block and frustration is expressed, which I don't think is a bad thing because we shouldn't be accepting this."

Report and free match highlights as Oli McBurnie's late double earns Hull a shock 2-0 Premier League victory over dominant Brighton following Costinha red card; Tigers goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis produces string of fine saves to deny visitors before added-time goals
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
A Konstantinos Tzolakis goalkeeping masterclass teed up Oli McBurnie to score two late goals as Hull stunned dominant Brighton in a smash-and-grab 2-0 win at the MKM Stadium.
Like the legendary Greek mythological king, Tzolakis had the Midas touch throughout for the Tigers, making five first-half saves - the most by any goalkeeper all season - before McBurnie netted twice in added time to snatch a victory that had looked beyond Hull for so long.
High-flying Brighton had racked up an xG of 2.24 and five presentable chances but were denied by a combination of the goalkeeper's fine form and some wasteful finishing, and ultimately missed the chance to move three points off leaders Arsenal.
Tzolakis' highlight was a stunning one-handed stop to keep out Diego Gomez's 15th-minute effort, which set the tone for a perfect performance to frustrate the visitors.
He was also at his best to deny Georginio Rutter, after Yasin Ayari's shot had rebounded off the crossbar, before a superb stop with his trailing leg frustrated Gomez again moments before the interval.
"We can be critical of some of the misses but the goalkeeper has been fantastic," said Sky Sports' Roy Keane at the break. "He's man of the match already for me."
With the one-way traffic unabated after the restart, Tzolakis owed some credit to midfielder Regan Slater for keeping his clean sheet intact, nodding off the line when substitute Charalampos Kostoulas lifted the ball over the goalkeeper after he had given the ball away cheaply himself.
The hosts did threaten with Mohamed Belloumi twice cutting in off the right before wasting good positions, and Sorba Thomas almost netting a fortuitous goal when his cross bounced back off the crossbar.
But, after Brighton's Costinha was shown a second yellow card for a clumsy challenge late on, Hull saw their moment to strike, with McBurnie scrambling in an opener following a counter-attack before tapping home a second with the Seagulls pushing to equalise.
Having been dropped by Greece during the international break following a 7-0 hammering by Netherlands, Tzolakis provided the perfect response with an unstoppable performance between the sticks.
The 24-year-old has been a hit on Humberside since his summer move from Olympiakos but was at his very best to earn them a first home win since August.
It was his second entry into the top 10 of xG prevented in individual matches this season, the only goalkeeper to manage such a feat.
Statistically, he performed better across 90 minutes in Hull's 1-0 win away at Coventry early in the campaign - another where their opponents had dominated - but his individual saves against the high-flying Seagulls were even more impressive.
They lifted him into fifth place in the season rankings of over-performing goalkeepers, ahead of Premier League greats Alisson and David Raya.
Though the Greek stopper would never claim to be on their level - yet - Hull increasingly look like they have a gem on their hands nonetheless.
"He [Tzolakis] was unbelievable, the cat today. He has been all season for us to be fair to him. We give him a bit of stick about his gear and that, but he's been good in net.
"He was fantastic, kept us in the game and that's how we want to play. We know if we are always in games we fancy ourselves to get chances and make it as horrible as possible and that's what we did."
"So many saves but two goals from Oli. It was a team effort and everyone helped each other.
"We are a unit here like a team. We play for each other. We saw a very good team effort, and we deserved to take the three points.
"In the first half we suffered a lot but we managed the second half and scored in transition two goals from Oli and that's it."
15: ONCE... Tzolakis begins his afternoon heroics by getting down low to keep out Gomez's effort.
19: MISS! Costinha should put Brighton ahead but fires wide from close range.
37: TWICE... Ayari's effort crashes off the bar before Rutter is again denied by Tzolakis on the follow-up.
45+3: THREE TIMES A 'KEEPER! Tzolakis keeps out another Gomez effort thanks to a superb stop with his trailing leg.
52: CLOSE! Gomez brings down a cross with a world-class first touch before lashing inches wide of the far post.
65: CLOSE! Against the run of play, Belloumi fires wide after leaving Olivier Boscagli on his backside.
79: OFF THE LINE! Kostoulas races through to latch onto Slater's backpass but the midfielder recovers to clear his chip off the line.
89: RED CARD! Costinha sees red for a clumsy lunge on Thomas, which earns him a second yellow card.
90+1: GOAL! McBurnie turns home an unlikely opener on the counter-attack to stun Brighton before...
90+4: GOAL! ...He adds a second from Belloumi's square ball to seal victory and send the MKM Stadium wild.

Report and free match highlights from the Championship match between Burnley and Blackburn Rovers at Turf Moor on Sunday; Burnley took the lead on two occasions but Blackburn battled back to draw; Rovers players sent a message to Tony Mowbray, in what would have been his 900th game
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Todd Cantwell's penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since head coach Tony Mowbray stepped back because of health issues.
In a gripping, physical east Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani's rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel's steered finish after the break.
But Andri Gudjohnsen scored Blackburn's first equaliser, then earned the penalty which Cantwell converted.
Burnley remain deep in relegation trouble, without a home league victory for 400 days, having once again failed to hold on to a lead. They have dropped 25 points from winning positions in the Sky Bet Championship this season.
Blackburn wanted a victory not just for local pride, but to honour Mowbray, who turned 63 on Sunday, and for whom this was set to be a 900th match in management before his announcement on Tuesday that he would be stepping back.
Their players warmed up in T-shirts bearing the message 'We're with you, Tony' on the back and the number 900 on the front.
Coaches Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds have taken charge in Mowbray's absence and had to reshuffle the defence when Tom Atcheson was concussed after receiving a boot to the face in the third minute.
Stand-in goalkeeper Aynsley Pears, playing after Balazs Toth suffered a broken hand on international duty with Hungary, pushed over a fierce deflected shot from Banel, but was at fault when Ramazani gave Burnley a 27th-minute lead.
The on-loan Leeds winger cut in from the right and fired a shot that flew into the roof of the net right by Pears, who was too slow to react.
But Gudjohnsen equalised four minutes later, racing on to a Harry Pickering long ball that drifted over Burnley centre-back Max Alleyne, and steering a sweet shot beyond goalkeeper Max Weiss for his 12th goal of the season. The Icelander celebrated by grabbing a t-shirt paying tribute to Mowbray from a photographer and displaying it for the cameras.
Blackburn finished the first half strongly, with Cantwell firing over a good chance, before Banel restored Burnley's lead six minutes into the second half, running unchallenged to place a shot into the far corner as defender Hayden Carter backed off.
The home side were fortunate to escape a strong penalty appeal just before the hour mark as Cantwell burst into the penalty area and saw two attempted crosses both strike the arm of Igor Julio.
Blackburn did get a penalty with 16 minutes left as Josh Laurent, attempting to clear a low cross, failed to spot Gudjohnsen darting in from behind him and caught the striker's leg. Cantwell drove the penalty straight down the middle to make it 2-2.
Gudjohnsen thought he had given Blackburn the lead two minutes later, when he controlled and drove a low shot against the base of the post with Weiss a spectator, but neither side could find a winner.
